bebe.q1: When you picture your life with a baby, your first reaction is…
bebe.q1a: A mix of excitement and calm, you feel ready to welcome that change.
bebe.q1b: Curiosity and desire, even if a few uncertainties remain.
bebe.q1c: Slight apprehension, you like the idea but it still feels abstract.
bebe.q1d: Anxiety or a mental block, you can't picture yourself in that role.
bebe.q2: Financially, how would you rate your current situation for welcoming a child?
bebe.q2a: You have solid savings, a stable income and you've already worked out what a baby costs.
bebe.q2b: Your situation is decent, you could adapt by reorganising some spending.
bebe.q2c: It's a bit tight, you'd need to shore up your finances before seriously considering it.
bebe.q2d: You're in a precarious financial situation and a child would add considerable stress.
bebe.q3: How would you describe your current relationship?
bebe.q3a: Solid, stable and fulfilling, you communicate well and get through hard times together.
bebe.q3b: Broadly good, with a few things to improve but nothing worrying.
bebe.q3c: Still being built or fragile on some points, communication could be better.
bebe.q3d: Unstable or non-existent, this isn't the right context to consider a baby.
bebe.q4: Are you ready to give up a large part of your sleep for several months?
bebe.q4a: Yes, you know it will be hard and you feel able to handle that tiredness.
bebe.q4b: You know it'll be tough but you think you can organise yourself to cope.
bebe.q4c: The idea of broken nights scares you a little, sleep matters a lot to you.
bebe.q4d: Not at all, you already struggle to function on little sleep.
bebe.q5: Do you have a support network (family, close friends) you could count on?
bebe.q5a: Yes, you have people nearby who are available and ready to help in practical ways.
bebe.q5b: You have a few trusted people, even if they're not all close by.
bebe.q5c: Your network is limited, you'd mostly have to rely on yourself.
bebe.q5d: You feel fairly isolated, there's no one you can really lean on.
bebe.q6: How do you see a baby affecting your career?
bebe.q6a: You have a clear plan: parental leave, return to work, childcare sorted.
bebe.q6b: You've thought about it without planning everything, but you know you'll find solutions.
bebe.q6c: It worries you, your work situation is still fragile or in transition.
bebe.q6d: You haven't thought about it at all, or your career is your absolute priority right now.
bebe.q7: How have you felt about your mental health these past few months?
bebe.q7a: Stable and settled, you handle your stress and emotions well day to day.
bebe.q7b: Pretty good, with normal ups and downs you know how to manage.
bebe.q7c: Fragile at times, you're going through a somewhat complicated period.
bebe.q7d: Difficult, you're dealing with anxiety, depression or significant burnout.
bebe.q8: Are you and your partner aligned on wanting a child?
bebe.q8a: Yes, you've talked about it openly and the desire is shared.
bebe.q8b: Broadly, even if the timing or some details still need discussing.
bebe.q8c: Not really, one of you is more enthusiastic than the other.
bebe.q8d: No, there's a clear disagreement or the subject has never come up.
bebe.q9a: You have suitable space, with a room available for a child.
bebe.q9b: Your current home could work for a while, even if moving would be ideal.
bebe.q9c: Your home is small or poorly suited, a change would be needed before a baby arrives.
bebe.q9d: Your housing situation is unstable or very precarious.
bebe.q10: Can you stay patient in stressful everyday situations?
bebe.q10a: Yes, you're fairly calm and patient, even under pressure.
bebe.q10b: Most of the time, though you have your limits like everyone.
bebe.q10c: You lose your temper quite easily and you know patience isn't your strong suit.
bebe.q10d: You often feel overwhelmed by stress, even over minor things.
bebe.q11: How do you react to a baby or young child crying around you?
bebe.q11a: You stay calm and naturally try to work out what's wrong.
bebe.q11b: It affects you, you do your best to help even when it isn't easy.
bebe.q11c: It makes you uncomfortable or stresses you out quickly.
bebe.q11d: It's completely beyond you, you'd rather move away.
bebe.q12: Are you ready to put some hobbies or passions on hold for the first few years?
bebe.q12a: Yes, you know it's temporary and you accept it calmly.
bebe.q12b: You're ready to adjust your pace, even if it takes some effort.
bebe.q12c: That sacrifice weighs on you just thinking about it.
bebe.q12d: No, your personal activities are essential to your balance and you don't want to give them up.
bebe.q13: Have you thought about the mental load and how parenting tasks would be shared?
bebe.q13a: Yes, you've discussed it as a couple and you have a clear view of the split.
bebe.q13b: You've thought about it and you know it matters, but nothing is settled yet.
bebe.q13c: Vaguely, you assume it'll sort itself out along the way.
bebe.q13d: Not at all, you have no idea what it involves in practice.
bebe.q14: How do you handle unexpected events and changes of plan in your life?
bebe.q14a: You adapt easily, surprises don't throw you.
bebe.q14b: You cope fine, though you prefer things planned.
bebe.q14c: Unexpected events stress you a lot and disrupt your daily life.
bebe.q14d: You need to control everything, the slightest change puts you in a difficult state.
bebe.q15: Do you feel emotionally mature enough to raise a child?
bebe.q15a: Yes, you've done real work on yourself and you know yourself well.
bebe.q15b: You think so, even if you know there are still things to work on.
bebe.q15c: You're not sure, you're still figuring yourself out in some areas.
bebe.q15d: No, you feel you still have a long way to go before being ready.
bebe.q16: What's your main motivation for having a child?
bebe.q16a: A deep, considered desire, driven by the wish to pass things on and accompany a new life.
bebe.q16b: The desire is growing naturally, you feel you're in a good phase of life for it.
bebe.q16c: Social or family pressure plays a part, even if there's some genuine desire.
bebe.q16d: You don't have a clear motivation, or you hope a baby would fill a void.
bebe.q17: Have you ever looked after a baby or young child for an extended period?
bebe.q17a: Yes, regularly, and it confirmed your desire.
bebe.q17b: A few times, and you did pretty well.
bebe.q17c: Very rarely, you don't have much experience with very young children.
bebe.q17d: Never, you have no idea what daily life with a baby looks like.
bebe.q18: How do you feel about your own childhood and the upbringing you received?
bebe.q18a: You've made peace with your past and you know what kind of parent you want to be, regardless of your models.
bebe.q18b: You've gained perspective, you want to repeat some things and avoid others.
bebe.q18c: It's a sensitive subject, some wounds haven't healed yet.
bebe.q18d: Your childhood was hard and you're afraid of repeating the same patterns.
bebe.q19: Are you ready to ask for help if you need it (doctor, therapist, people around you)?
bebe.q19a: Absolutely, you know asking for help is a strength, not a weakness.
bebe.q19b: You think so, even if it isn't always easy for you.
bebe.q19c: You'd struggle, you generally prefer to manage on your own.
bebe.q19d: No, asking for help feels impossible or shameful to you.
bebe.q20: If you had to sum up how you feel about having a baby now…
bebe.q20a: You feel confident and enthusiastic, the conditions are there to go for it.
bebe.q20b: You're fairly positive, a few details remain but the essentials are in place.
bebe.q20c: You're hesitating, some important things aren't in place yet.
bebe.q20d: You feel it isn't the right time, and it's okay to acknowledge that.
bebe.r1_d: Based on your answers, several important parts of your life aren't yet aligned for welcoming a baby. Whether emotionally, financially, relationally or personally, there are fragile areas. This is neither a failure nor a judgement: it's simply a snapshot of where you are right now.
bebe.r1_a: Not being ready today doesn't mean never being ready. Take the time to shore up what needs it, whether that's your financial stability, your mental health or your relationship. The time you give yourself is a gift to your future child.
bebe.r2_d: You're not fully ready yet, but the desire is starting to take form. Some areas of your life are solid, others still need work. This is a normal and healthy phase: you're thinking it through seriously rather than rushing in.
bebe.r2_a: Identify the two or three things holding you back most and focus on those. Talk openly about your doubts with your partner, or with someone you trust. The goal isn't to reach perfection, but to feel solid enough to take the leap.
bebe.r3_d: Most of the lights are green. You've clearly thought this through, your life is fairly stable and your desire seems genuine. A few minor adjustments remain, but nothing that should hold you back for long.
bebe.r3_a: The last details to sort out (housing, organisation, conversations with your partner) can be worked on over the coming weeks or months. Don't wait for everything to be perfect, perfection doesn't exist in parenting. Trust your ability to adapt.
bebe.r4_d: Your answers show real maturity and solid preparation. Emotional, financial and relational stability: the foundations are there. Your desire seems considered, sincere and shared. That's an excellent signal.
bebe.r4_a: If the desire is there and the conditions allow it, there's no reason to wait indefinitely. The perfect moment doesn't exist, but a good moment is recognisable. Make the most of that energy and keep talking with your partner so you move forward together.
